item.content:encoded:
Tongan sprinter Hunter Jahnke has broken Tonga's national men's 100 metres record after producing a personal best performance on the opening day of the World Athletics Under-20 Championships in Oregon, United States.

The 19-year-old clocked 10.58 seconds in Heat 1 to finish eighth, lowering Tonga's previous national record of 10.90 seconds and his previous personal best of 10.87, setting a new personal best.

Jahnke is Tonga's sole representative at the championships, being held at Hayward Field from August 5-9, where more than 1,800 athletes from 147 member federations are competing.

Tonga Athletics Association vice-president, Pilimilose Feke, told Matangi Tonga today, that Jahnke earned his place at the championships after travelling to Tonga from Australia to compete at the national secondary schools intercollegiate athletics competition held earlier in April of this year.

" Hunter came to Tonga and competed in the intercollegiate sports, winning gold in the Open Boys 60-metre division, which qualified him for the World Under-20 Athletics Championships," Feke said.

The Tonga Athletics Association president, 'Alifeleti Tu'ihalamaka, travelled to the United States with Jahnke, who is the country's only athlete competing at the championships. The Association also acknowledged Valerie Adams and her support for Hunter during his preparation for the competition.

The event marks the 40 th anniversary of the World Athletics Under-20 Championships and has attracted a record number of competitors, surpassing the previous record of 1,558 athletes set in Lima in 2024.

Feke said, Tonga initially qualified two athletes for the championships, with shot putter Penisimani Ta'e'iloa also earning selection. Ta'e'iloa secured qualification at the Oceania Athletics Championships in Darwin, Australia, in May.

" However, Penisimani Ta'eiloa's visa application was not lodged in time due to his selection to represent Tonga at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Unfortunately, he could not make it to the competition with Hunter."
